metaDescription: Conference speakerphones compared on microphone arrays, USB versus Bluetooth, certification and room size, so everyone in the meeting can be heard clearly.
expertTake: The Jabra Speak2 55 is the best overall pick because four beamforming microphones, a strong speaker and Bluetooth plus USB connection cover most small meeting rooms. The Jabra Speak 410 is the value pick, a corded USB speakerphone that works with any computer and needs no battery. Anyone running meetings for large rooms should skip tabletop speakerphones and look at a room system with ceiling or bar microphones, because a single puck cannot cover many seats.
introParagraphs: A conference speakerphone puts a speaker and microphones in a single unit for a table, so a group can join a call without headsets. The hard part is hearing everyone at the table, not just the person closest to the unit.

This guide compares speakerphones for small and medium meeting spaces and home offices. We evaluated each on published specifications, microphone arrays, connection options, certification and owner feedback patterns, and we explain where a single unit stops being enough.

products.name: Jabra Speak2 55 Wireless Bluetooth Speakerphone, 4 Beamforming Mics
products.description:
The Jabra Speak2 55 is a portable speakerphone with four beamforming microphones that pick up voices from all directions. The 2025 edition adds a USB-C charging adaptor, and it connects over Bluetooth or USB. It is the premium option in this guide and the one with the strongest array.

Beamforming lets the unit focus on whoever is speaking, which helps when several people sit around a table. Compared with the Speak 510, it offers a stronger speaker and a more capable microphone array. Compared with the Anker S330, it adds Bluetooth and portability with a battery. It suits a small meeting room or a home office with visitors.

In use, place the unit in the middle of the table, away from laptop fans and projectors. Set it as the default audio device in your meeting software, and check the volume level before the meeting. The battery will age, so keep it plugged in for long sessions. Update the firmware through the maker's software, which can improve call quality.
products.bestFor: Small meeting rooms and home offices that need a portable wireless speakerphone with a strong mic array.

Bluetooth and USB connection options
USB-C charging adaptor included in the 2025 edition
Portable for moving between rooms
cons: Highest cost tier in the lineup
Battery ages and long sessions need power

products.name: Jabra Speak 410 USB Corded Speakerphone, Plug and Play
products.description:
The Jabra Speak 410 is a corded USB speakerphone that plugs into a computer and works with softphones and meeting software. There is no battery, no pairing and no app. It sits at the low end of this guide's cost range and has been a go-to for small rooms for years.

The corded design is its strength: no charging, no Bluetooth dropouts and a simple setup. Compared with the Speak2 55, it has fewer microphones and no wireless connection, so it suits a table with a computer near it. Compared with the Anker S330, it is similar in concept, and the choice often comes down to preference. It is a good fit for a huddle of a few people around a laptop.

Ownership is straightforward. Plug it in, select it as the audio device and place it centrally. The cord limits placement, and USB-A may need an adapter on newer laptops. Without modern noise handling, background noise can leak into calls in a busy room.
products.bestFor: Small groups around a laptop who want a low-cost, plug-in speakerphone with no battery.
pros: Lowest cost tier with a long record
Plug and play with no battery or pairing
USB powered and works with softphones
Simple and reliable for small huddles
cons: Fewer microphones and basic noise handling
USB-A may need an adapter on newer laptops

products.name: Anker PowerConf S330 USB Speakerphone, 360 Degree Voice Pickup

specList.label: Processing
specList.value: Voice enhancement and background noise reduction

products.description:
The Anker PowerConf S330 is a USB speakerphone for home offices that connects over USB-C and includes a standard USB adapter. It offers 360 degree voice pickup and voice enhancement that suppresses background noise while boosting voices. It is a plug-and-play solution that joins meetings in seconds.

The voice enhancement is the useful feature for a home office where background noise from a street or a fan can leak into calls. Compared with the Jabra Speak 410, it adds modern noise processing and a USB-C connection. Compared with the Speak2 55, it is cabled and has no Bluetooth, which makes it simpler and cheaper. It suits one to a few people.

In practice, place it on the desk near the speakers, and choose it as the default device in your meeting app. USB-C and adapters add connection points that can loosen. The cabled design is reliable, but it ties the unit to the computer. For small groups, check that the pickup covers everyone, since a single puck has limits.
products.bestFor: Home office workers and small huddles who want modern noise handling with a simple cable.

Plug and play over USB-C with a USB-A adapter
Noise reduction helps in a noisy home office
Low to mid cost tier
cons: Cabled design ties it to the computer
Single unit has limited coverage for larger groups

products.name: Jabra Speak 510 (2025 Edition) Portable USB and Bluetooth Speakerphone
products.description:
The Jabra Speak 510 (2025 edition) is a portable speakerphone that connects by USB or Bluetooth and is built for meetings and calls. The maker highlights clear audio and quick setup. It is a step up from the corded Speak 410 because it adds wireless flexibility.

It sits between the 410 and the Speak2 55 in the Jabra line. Compared with the Speak 410, it adds Bluetooth and a portable design. Compared with the Speak2 55, it has fewer microphones and a more modest feature set, with a lower cost. It is a good choice for people who move between a desk and a conference table.

Ownership is easy: pair by Bluetooth with a phone, or plug into a laptop by USB. Keep it charged, and place it in the center of the table. A wireless speakerphone suffers when the battery is low, so charge before important meetings. The microphone array is built for small groups, not large rooms.
products.bestFor: People who split time between desk and meeting room and want a Jabra speakerphone with Bluetooth.
pros: USB and Bluetooth connection options
Portable with quick setup
Jabra audio quality for calls
Mid-tier cost from an established brand
cons: Battery needs charging for wireless use

products.name: EMEET Luna Plus Kit Conference Speaker with Satellite Microphone, 8+1 Mics
products.description:
The EMEET Luna Plus kit includes a conference speaker and a dedicated satellite microphone, for 8 plus 1 microphones in total with 360 degree pickup. The maker calls it its first Bluetooth speakerphone with a satellite mic. The satellite extends the pickup to a second spot, which helps with a longer table.

The satellite microphone is the practical difference. Compared with the Jabra Speak2 55, it offers more microphones and a way to cover a longer table. Compared with the Yealink SP92, it is more of a kit than a single device. It suits meeting rooms where one puck cannot reach everyone.

In use, place the main unit in the middle and the satellite at the far end of the table, so every seat has a nearby mic. Connect by Bluetooth or USB, and set it as the default audio device. The satellite adds a cable or wireless link to manage, and more parts to charge or lose. Check the manual for how many people it is intended to serve.
products.bestFor: Longer tables where one speakerphone cannot reach every seat.

8 plus 1 microphones with 360 degree coverage
Bluetooth and USB connection

cons: Extra part to place, power and keep track of

products.name: Yealink SP92 Conference Speaker and Microphone, Teams Certified
products.description:
The Yealink SP92 is a conference speaker with a 50 mm speaker, a 360 degree omnidirectional microphone, AI noise cancelling and Microsoft Teams certification. The maker lists up to 20 hours of call time. It is aimed at small to medium rooms and managed corporate setups.

Teams certification matters in offices where IT teams require certified hardware, since it confirms integration with Teams controls. Compared with the Jabra Speak2 55, it targets enterprise buyers with certification and a larger speaker. Compared with the Anker S330, it is a bigger unit with more battery. It is less about home use and more about the meeting room.

Ownership is about the usual routine: charge it, place it in the center of the table and set it as the default device. A 20 hour call claim is a manufacturer figure, and real life depends on volume and use. Check firmware through the maker's tools, and confirm that your meeting app recognizes the unit. If you are not in a Teams environment, the certification adds less.
products.bestFor: Teams-based offices that want a certified speakerphone with a larger speaker.

50 mm speaker fills a small room
AI noise cancelling and 360 degree mic
Up to 20 hours of call time claimed
cons: Certification matters mostly in Teams environments

buyingCriteria.explanation: A single speakerphone suits a small group around one table, usually a handful of people. A longer table needs a kit with an extra microphone, such as the EMEET Luna Plus satellite. Large rooms need a ceiling or bar system. The common mistake is buying a personal speakerphone for a room that needs more coverage. Count the seats at the far end of the table, because that is where pickup fails first, and place the unit so no one sits more than a short reach away.

More microphones help only if the processing is good. The Jabra Speak2 55 uses four beamforming mics, and the EMEET lists 8 plus 1. Beamforming focuses on the current speaker. The Jabra Speak 410 has a simpler design. Evaluate coverage, echo handling and noise suppression together, not the microphone count alone. Listen to a recording of a test call with two people talking, since overlapping speech is where weak arrays struggle.

USB is the most reliable and avoids pairing, as with the Jabra Speak 410 and Anker S330. Bluetooth adds flexibility for phones and laptops, as with the Speak2 55 and Speak 510, but adds pairing and battery management. Having both is the most flexible. Check what your computer ports support. If you share the unit between computers, a USB cable you can unplug and move is easier than re-pairing Bluetooth.

Teams or Zoom certification means the maker has confirmed integration with call controls. The Yealink SP92 is Teams certified. In managed offices, certification can be a requirement. At home, any USB device that appears as an audio device will work. Check that firmware updates are available.

The speaker must be loud enough for the room without distortion, and full duplex handling lets people talk at the same time without cutting each other off. A 50 mm driver, as on the Yealink SP92, is larger than the small speakers on personal pucks. For small rooms, clarity matters more than volume.

Wireless units depend on a battery, and claims like the Yealink 20 hours are maker figures. Corded USB units, such as the Jabra Speak 410 and Anker S330, never run out. For regular meetings, a unit that can stay plugged in is simpler. Plan charging for portable units. A unit that charges over USB-C can share a charger with your laptop or phone.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pickup and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared microphone arrays, from the four beamforming mics of the Jabra Speak2 55 to the 8 plus 1 of the EMEET Luna Plus. Coverage claims were treated as claims. Our scores are editorial assessments based on published specifications and owner feedback patterns.

howWeEvaluated.title: Connection
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared USB, Bluetooth and dual connections and weighed reliability against flexibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speaker and clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We read speaker sizes, such as the 50 mm driver on the Yealink SP92, and noise handling, such as the Anker voice enhancement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Certification and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered Teams certification and which environments need it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged each unit by relative cost tier and avoided price figures. Room-size limits were stated plainly.

cards.label: Corded USB
cards.text: The Jabra Speak 410 and Anker S330 need no battery and give the most reliable connection.

cards.label: Wireless
cards.text: The Speak2 55, Speak 510 and Yealink SP92 move between rooms, but rely on batteries and pairing.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded for a fixed desk. Choose wireless if you move between rooms.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Microphone coverage that matches your seats, echo cancellation, a connection that suits your computer and a unit you can place centrally.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Jabra Speak2 55 leads on balance, the Speak 410 on value and the EMEET Luna Plus on table length.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You run meetings daily, have a longer table or need certification. The Speak2 55 or Yealink pays back in clarity.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have occasional small calls. The Speak 410 or Anker S330 is enough.

maintenance.why: Distance from speakers affects pickup. Put the unit in the middle of the table, away from fans and projectors.
Updates can improve noise handling and fix bugs. Use the maker's software. Check the release notes to see what changed before you install.
Wireless units drop out when the battery is low. Keep them plugged in for long sessions.
Meeting apps can switch to the laptop speakers. Confirm the speakerphone is selected.
Dust and dirt reduce clarity. Wipe gently with a dry cloth.

faq.q: How many people can one speakerphone cover?
faq.a: A single unit suits a small group around a table. Larger groups need a kit with extra microphones or a room system. Seat distance matters as much as seat count, so measure the table before you decide.

faq.q: Is Bluetooth good enough for meetings?
faq.a: Usually, but USB is more reliable. Bluetooth adds pairing and battery management.

faq.q: Do I need a certified speakerphone?
faq.a: Only in managed offices that require it. At home, any USB audio device works.

faq.q: Why do others hear an echo?
faq.a: Echo happens when speaker sound feeds back into a microphone. Lower the volume, keep other devices muted and use a unit with echo cancellation. Using a headset for the other participants on the same call in the room also causes feedback, so use only one audio device per room.

faq.q: Can I use it with my phone?
faq.a: Bluetooth models like the Jabra Speak2 55 and Speak 510 can pair with a phone. Corded USB models cannot.
Corded units last many years. Wireless batteries age, and speaker clarity depends on keeping the grille clean.
